home.card.swordland: Thirty players, one hour, one map. Who does what, and when.
sl.title: Swordland Showdown
sl.thesis: {legions} Legions of {n}, {subs} in reserve each, {zones} zones, one mission. Everyone goes in knowing where they belong, what they hold and who they follow. We do not work out assignments after the whistle.
sl.roster.title: Who takes the field
sl.roster.lede: A Legion is {mains} main fighters plus {subs} substitutes. Only the top {top} alliances by power can register at all, so a seat is never guaranteed just because you signed up.
sl.roster.subs: Main slots nobody claims open to the {subs} substitutes {n} minutes into the match, first come first served. If you are a substitute, be online at the start anyway.
sl.legions.head: An alliance can register {n} Legions.
sl.legions.body: Alliance rewards follow Legion 1's result and nothing else. Legion 2 can win its own match and it does not change the alliance payout.
sl.legions.do: Legion 1 takes the stronger accounts. Take a Legion 2 seat anyway — personal rewards follow your own Relic Point rank in either one.
sl.phases.title: How the hour runs
sl.phases.lede: {minutes} minutes, three phases. Each one puts something new on the map, and the new thing is always worth more than what came before.
sl.phases.warn: Only the wave times are still unread. Everything else here comes off the match itself.
phase.one.title: Take the cheap ground
phase.one.body: Sanctums, Abbeys, the Bell Tower and the Royal Stables are all open from the whistle. The Stables cut every teleport that follows from {tp} minutes to {tpFast}, which is worth more than the points on any single building.
phase.two.title: The Swordshrine and the Hall open
phase.two.body: The Swordshrine, the Hall of Reformation and the Mercenary Camp unlock together. The Hall raises the combat power everything after it is fought with. The Shrine is the biggest point source on the map and it is under constant mercenary attack, so holding it this early usually means handing it straight back — but its first capture is a one-off you keep even when you lose the building.
phase.three.title: Undercellar waves
phase.three.body: Undercellars arrive in {waves} waves and pay out for plain gathering, with no fight required.
sl.points.title: Worth knowing
sl.points.q: Should I defend a building or go and hit someone?
sl.points.a: Hit someone. Defeating enemy troops pays about {attackPay} Relic Points per 10,000 power on offence against about {defendPay} defending — roughly {payRatio}× for the same troops. Defend only while the building is actually generating for you.
sl.first.title: First capture pays once
sl.first.lede: The first alliance to fully occupy a building, once its capture timer completes, takes the one-time bonus in the table above — in both alliance and personal points. It is paid once per building for the whole match, and then it is gone for everyone.
sl.first.head: A first capture cannot be taken back.
sl.first.body: Occupation points bank on the building, and {pct}% of them are still sitting there for whoever flips it next. The first-capture bonus does not work that way. It pays the moment the building becomes yours and it stays paid even if you lose the building a minute later.
bonus.weaken: Weakens attack and defence on enemy garrisons
sl.pay.title: What every building pays
sl.pay.lede: Two numbers per building: the one-time bonus for taking it first, then the rate it pays every minute you keep it. Alliance and personal points are counted separately and you earn both at the same time.
sl.pay.note: Four Abbeys, two Sanctums, one of everything else.
sl.pay.head: Both Sanctums beat the Swordshrine — {bothSanctums} a minute against {shrineRate}.
sl.pay.body: The Shrine is the richest single building on the map, but there is only one of it. Two Sanctums pay {bothSanctums} alliance points a minute between them, against the Shrine's {shrineRate}, and they are open from the whistle instead of a quarter of an hour in.
sl.first.egq: Is the Swordshrine worth taking if we cannot hold it?
sl.first.ega: Yes. Being first into the Shrine pays {shrineFirst} to the alliance and {shrineFirstYou} to you, and you keep every point of that even if you lose it thirty seconds later. Holding it is a separate {shrineRate} a minute.
sl.lock.title: The first {n} minutes
sl.lock.lede: Joining does not let you act. The map is locked for about {n} minutes. Use it to send reinforcements.
sl.zones.title: The order of battle
sl.zones.lede: The map is cut into {zones} zones and all {n} starters belong to one of them. Find your name, learn the two or three around it, and you are ready.
sl.zones.shared: {shrine} belongs to no zone. It is a Legion objective, and leadership calls the rotation onto it as the battle develops.
zone.name: {zone} Zone
zone.purple.name: Purple
zone.blue.name: Blue
zone.green.name: Green
zone.yellow.name: Yellow
zone.purple.flex: Join Purple rallies, reinforce Purple members and buildings, and take the Undercellars and Loot that appear in Purple. Be ready to drop all of it and reinforce.
zone.blue.flex: Reinforce Blue members, join every Blue rally, and keep the Blue garrisons topped up. Gather and loot around that, never instead of it.
zone.green.flex: Reinforce each other and keep reinforcements standing in the Green buildings. Gather and loot only while Green is quiet.
zone.yellow.flex: Fill the Yellow garrisons immediately, then reinforce each other. Gather and loot when there is room, and go straight back to garrison duty.
sl.flex.title: If you are Flex
sl.flex.lede: Four jobs, in this order. When two of them want you at the same time, the one higher up the list wins.
sl.flex.fallback: No rally, no Loot, no Undercellar needing you? Reinforce your zone's garrisons. That is the default, not standing still.
flex.rally.title: Join every rally in your zone
flex.rally.body: Not the ones you like the look of — every one. A rally that launches short is worth less than one that waited ten seconds for you.
flex.reinforce.title: Keep your zone reinforced
flex.reinforce.body: Your zone's buildings and the people holding them. One march can only go to one player, so spread out instead of everyone stacking on the same name.
flex.gather.title: Gather Undercellars
flex.gather.body: They pay for plain gathering with no fight attached, which makes them close to free points — but only while nothing in your zone needs you.
flex.loot.title: Grab the Loot in your zone
flex.loot.body: Same rule. Take it when it appears in your colour, and drop it first the moment your zone comes under pressure.
sl.reserve.title: The ready reserve
sl.reserve.lede: Main slots nobody claims open to the substitutes a few minutes in, first come first served.
sl.reserve.head: Substitutes are not spectators.
sl.reserve.body: You can be activated into any of the four zones, and nobody will brief you when it happens. Know the whole plan — every zone, every lead, every objective — not only the one you expect to land in.
sl.reserve.do: If you are called: report to that zone’s lead, say you are in, and take over the position of whoever you replaced. Be online at the start whether or not you expect a slot.
sl.orders.title: Legion-wide orders
sl.orders.lede: These outrank everything else on this page. When two of them pull against each other, the lower number wins.
order.objectives.title: Objectives come first
order.objectives.body: Players with a named building lock it down and stay on it. Everyone else reinforces, rallies, gathers and loots around them. That is the shape of the whole match.
order.secondary.title: Undercellars and Loot are secondary
order.secondary.body: They are points with no fight attached, which is exactly what makes them tempting. If your zone comes under pressure, stop gathering and reinforce — immediately, not once this one finishes.
order.nofreelance.title: Do not freelance
order.nofreelance.body: Stay inside your assignment unless your zone lead or Legion leadership moves you. Never leave a building or a reinforcement position to chase points somewhere else.
order.shrine.title: The {shrine} is called, not rushed
order.shrine.body: It is a shared Legion objective. No zone abandons its own responsibilities to rush the centre on its own initiative. Leadership decides when we shift pressure there, and which zones move.
sl.chain.title: Chain of command
sl.chain.lede: If you do not know what to do, do what your zone lead says.
sl.chain.note: Know your zone. Know your objective. Reinforce your team. Follow the calls.
sl.map.title: The battlefield
sl.map.lede: Four zones around a shared centre. {shrine} sits in the middle and belongs to nobody — everything else is inside somebody’s colour.
sl.map.cap: Zone boundaries and building positions, from the Legion 1 operation order. Labels are in English on the map itself; every building is named in your language elsewhere on this page.
sl.map.alt: Map of the Swordland arena, divided into four coloured zones around a central Swordshrine.
sl.map.cellars: The {n} Undercellars spawn in {zones} only. The other two zones have none of their own — if you are Flex there and the call goes out to gather, ask your zone lead before you leave your colour.

sl.zones.synced: Names, ranks and faces pulled from MightPulse on {date}.
order.communicate.title: Say what you can see
order.communicate.body: Enemy movements, incoming attacks, an empty garrison, a building about to flip — call it. A zone lead can only direct what somebody tells them about, and the thing you assume everyone noticed is usually the thing nobody did.
order.nowaste.title: Do not waste marches
order.nowaste.body: Every march sent somewhere pointless is one that is not defending a building when the hit lands. Move with a reason, and let the cooldown you save be the one that matters later.
